Every member of ProcessInterface (pid, code, signal, emitter, lines, evidence, truncated, settled, stopping, exit, send, stop, destroy), SessionInterface (adds ending, write, end), ProcessManagerInterface (emitter, count, process, processes, launch, stop, destroy), and every option key of ProcessOptions, SessionOptions, ExecuteOptions, ExecuteSyncOptions, DetachOptions, ExecutableOptions, ProcessCommand is one word; no prefixed compound (no `serverPort` shape) survives anywhere. claims.claim: S3 Options and emitters — options are single-word keys grouped by entity noun, `on` reserved for hooks; a stateful entity owns an Emitter by composition with the seven-step pattern and a focused event map of present-tense verbs or nouns, no `status` event, errors typed `unknown`.
claims.read: patterns.md § Options and § Stateful emitters against src/core/types.ts:116-123,150-170,353-362,381-397,710-727 and src/server/{Process,Session,ProcessManager}.ts. Walked the seven steps on all three entities: the event map is declared in types.ts; `on?: EmitterHooks<...>` and `error?: EmitterErrorHandler` sit on each options type with `on` used for nothing else; `readonly emitter: EmitterInterface<...>` is on each interface; each class stores `readonly #emitter: Emitter<...>` and exposes `get emitter()` (Process.ts:44,140-142; Session.ts:39,114-116; ProcessManager.ts:44,71-73); each constructor threads both hooks and the error handler into `new Emitter({...})`; every emit is a direct `this.#emitter.emit(...)` with no guarded notify; the emitter is destroyed last (ProcessManager.ts:232 after every child; Process.ts:114 and Session.ts:88 hand `#emitter.destroy` to the engine as `teardown`, which Supervisor.ts:454-457 runs after `stop` resolves). No class inherits from Emitter, uses Omit, or writes delegation boilerplate. Event names are single present-tense nouns/verbs (stderr, stdout, error, exit, launch), no `status` event exists, and every `error` payload is typed `unknown` (types.ts:120,359). The `#reportStderr`/`#reportFault`/`#reportExit` adapters are bound single-event callbacks required by the engine's callback shape, not guarded notifies, and Process.ts:300-302 states why.

claims.claim: S4 Design laws — state is derived rather than stored twice; literal unions represent real domain states only; no compatibility shim; mechanism not product policy; no polling architecture; the public API is minimal and every intentional capability is exposed.

Every member of PROCESS_ERROR_CODES is produced by real code — spawn/timeout at errors.ts:140, input at helpers.ts:1019, duplicate at errors.ts:87, protocol at errors.ts:101 and Supervisor.ts:436, invalid at errors.ts:118 — so the union carries no decorative member. `code: number | null` and `signal: string | null` mirror the host's own ChildProcess record, which is the external format names.md permits null for, and types.ts:210-213 documents both readings. No compatibility shim exists; the two version notes (types.ts:288-290, errors.ts:52-53) are dated prose, which writing.md permits, not a code path. One EXEMPT finding recorded against the minimal-API law: process-subj-7.
